case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Expect slow pier salmon fishing this week everywhere.** Rating for the week: South Haven 1, St. Joseph 1, Grand Haven 0, Muskegon 0.
- **Go to South Haven.** It has the highest recent pier rating, and it is the one port whose buoy shows a sharp drop, which may mean upwelling.
- **If you can, fish early or late in low light, casting spoons.** That is what the few pier catches were on.
- **If pier results stay slow, switch to a boat.** Boats were doing better than piers at every port in the latest reports.

## Why
- The most recent pier reports were all slow: Grand Haven's Oct 9 report rated pier salmon fishing 0 (slow).
- South Haven's Oct 1 pier report was the only pier rating above 0 (1, below average), with a couple of salmon caught on spoons.
- I'd expect a sharp buoy drop to bring fish toward the piers, so South Haven's possible upwelling is the best reason to pick it, though the pier reports don't show that yet.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (newest is Oct 9, five days old):**
- South Haven, Oct 1: pier rated 1 (below average). "Pier fishing was a little slow. … There were a couple of salmon caught by anglers casting spoons."
- Grand Haven, Oct 9: pier rated 0 (slow). "Pier anglers targeting salmon found the action to be slow."
- Muskegon, Oct 1: pier rated 0 (slow). "Pier anglers also found the salmon action to be slow." Muskegon's Sept 17 pier report was also 0.
- St. Joseph, Sept 24: pier rated 0 (slow), with shrimp the only catch and warm water around the pier heads. Oct 1 said "the piers were a little slow" without a rating.
- No pier report at all for Muskegon or South Haven on Oct 9, or for St. Joseph after Oct 1.
- Boats (for comparison): Grand Haven Oct 9 found fish 40–90 ft down in 80–160 ft of water on spoons. St. Joseph Oct 9 rated boats 1 and called it "very inconsistent." South Haven Oct 9 rated boats 1 in 60–100 ft of water.

**Conditions now (buoy, measured, week before Oct 14):**
- South Haven: 61 F, down 3 F over the week, flagged as a possible upwelling.
- St. Joseph: 58 F, down 4 F.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon: 63 F, down 4 F.
- The tool returned a backtest summary, not live data, and gave no pierhead water temperature or wind forecast. I can't tell you the pier water or this weekend's wind.

**Past seasons:** I didn't pull earlier-season matches this time, so nothing here is historical.

## Caveats
- The newest report is five days old, and the Oct 9 reports came from a period when the buoys were already showing a sharp drop. Conditions may have changed since.
- The ratings are my estimate from a handful of pier mentions, not a full pier survey. Pier reports are sparse, especially for Muskegon and South Haven on Oct 9.
- Buoys are offshore. The South Haven and St. Joseph drops suggest upwelling, but they don't measure pier water directly.
- Wind isn't in the data. Check the forecast before heading out, especially if you're considering a boat.

## Sources
- Oct 9 DNR report: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3f6328e
- Oct 1 DNR report: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3f5314a
- Sept 24 DNR report: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3f41b68
- Sept 17 DNR report: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3f30d9c
